How to open clipboard history on Windows

Press Windows + V to see your clipboard history. If it is your first time, choose Turn on. The history starts collecting new copies after you enable it.

Reviewed 29 October 2026 · Clipora editorial

On this page
Start with Windows + VPin the copies you need againWhy an earlier copy might be missingWhen a searchable library helpsKnow which history you are clearing

Start with Windows + V

  1. Click the input or document where you want to paste.
  2. Press Windows + V. Choose Turn on if prompted.
  3. Copy a short, non-sensitive sentence with Ctrl + C. Copy a second sentence.
  4. Open Windows + V again and select the earlier item.

If history is disabled, open Settings → System → Clipboard → Clipboard history. An organization-managed computer may restrict this setting.

Pin the copies you need again

Open an item’s menu and choose Pin. Microsoft documents a 25-item history, with up to 4 MB per item. Supported formats include text, HTML and bitmap images. Older unpinned items are removed as the history fills.

Pinned items survive a restart. Ordinary history does not. Pinning is useful for a short address or a frequently used reply, but a clipboard should not become a password vault.

Why an earlier copy might be missing

  • It was copied before history was enabled.
  • It was unpinned when Windows restarted, or it aged out of the history.
  • Its format or size is unsupported, or the originating app marks it private.
  • You are looking at another computer’s history without compatible sync enabled.

Turning history on now cannot recover content that was never recorded. Check the original document, message or application instead.

When a searchable library helps

Windows history is a useful place to start. If you repeatedly hunt for older text, links or images, Clipora adds a persistent searchable library, collections and a resizable quick-access picker.

Keep Clipora running, copy a harmless sample, then press Ctrl + Alt + V. Type part of the sample and select it. Clipora records new copies while running and unpaused; it does not import Windows history.

Try the sample history in your browser or follow the Windows app quick start.

Know which history you are clearing

Windows history and a clipboard manager’s history are separate. Clearing one does not clear the other. Read the clipboard clearing guide before removing sensitive copies.

Windows instructions: Microsoft’s clipboard guide. Reviewed 29 October 2026. Labels can vary with your Windows build.
